text: Project Title: Computer-Assisted V erification: An Investigation into Proof Assistants and Formal Mathematical Reasoning Student Name: William Fayers Supervisor: Dr. Yuri Santos Rego Email: YSantosRego@lincoln.ac.uk Module: MTH3011/MTH3005 Submission Date: 27 October 2025 Mathematics derives its foundational power from rigorous logical deduction. However , despite centuries of refinement, even published proofs by experienced mathematicians occasionally contain errors, gaps, or ambiguities that undermine their validity . The seminal example of the Needham-Schroeder authentication protocol—which remained unquestioned for nearly a decade before researchers discovered critical security flaws—demonstrates that logical errors can persist even in carefully scrutinized work. Similarly, monumental results such as the Feit-Thompson theorem span hundreds of pages of dense argumentation, making human verification extraordinarily challenging. This project investigates formal methods in mathematics : the use of computer-assisted proof verification systems to establish mathematical truth with unprecedented rigor . Proof assistants such as Lean, Coq, and the Prototype V erification System (PVS) provide mechanized frameworks based on higher-order logic and dependent type theory , enabling mathematicians to construct machine-checkable proofs that eliminate ambiguity through computers' inherently boolean nature. My research will explore the logical foundations of formal verification, examine contemporary proof assistants and their applications, and undertake hands-on formalization of mathematical theorems. This interdisciplinary work intersects mathematical logic, computer science, and formal verification—domains that align with my background as a mathematics undergraduate with extensive programming experience in Python and other languages. Personal Motivation: Having developed complex software systems and witnessed firsthand the challenges of ensuring correctness in computational systems, I am particularly drawn to the intersection of mathematical rigor and computational verification. My experience with network infrastructure configuration and debugging has reinforced the importance of formal specifications and rigorous validation. This project of fers an opportunity to explore how mathematical foundations can provide guarantees of correctness that testing alone cannot achieve.
